_about: Programs and services a company can put behind one tier of the decision chain. decidecall runs none of them itself: each becomes an adapter (a command the company installs and names in decidecall-adapters.json). Every row says where it was read and on which day; 'status' is 'verified' when the repository or package page itself was opened, 'secondary' when only another site says it.

candidates.what: A 1.9B decision model (Qwen3.5-2B torso with a pointer head): picks an option or rates on a scale in one forward pass, with a calibrated confidence. CLI `strands-decider ask` and a server with POST /v1/systemone.
candidates.claims: answers at confidence 0.9 or more are right about 95% of the time on unseen short classification tasks; JevBench v1 (public set) accuracy 0.723 (167 of 231); median 115 ms on an RTX 3090 (the repository's README)

candidates.what: An open, Jev-compatible decision server on DiffusionGemma: POST /v1/systemone {state, model, questions} -> {model, answers, usage}; question types noul, choice, score; confidence = 1 - H(p)/ln K.
An open-weight alternative to TypeSafe Jev: typed decisions with a probability for every option in one forward pass (Qwen3.5-4B with a LoRA distilled from Qwen3.6-27B); served through OpenJev.

TypeSafe's hosted decision model Jev (released 15.09.2026, early access): POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, model jev-latest. $42 per billion input tokens, output free; no zero-data-retention option.
candidates.note: Price from TypeSafe's announcement as carried by DataCamp: $42 per billion input tokens ($0.042 per million), output free, early access. Plan rule (JEV 92.txt): pay for it only after bench shows it beats cache + rules + a local model. Reach it with the example adapter: the key comes from the keychain, never from the file.

candidates.what: A plugin for Simon Willison's `llm` command-line tool that reaches TypeSafe models; a ready command line for the systemone adapter.
candidates.note: PyPI version 0.1a0 (alpha) on the day it was read; needs the company's own TypeSafe key.

candidates.what: Few-shot sentence-transformer classifiers: train a small local classifier from a few dozen labelled examples (decidecall's journal of human answers is such a set).
Structured generation for local models: forces the answer into a JSON Schema, a regex or a fixed set of choices - the outputSchema of an adapter enforced at generation time.
Grammar-constrained decoding used inside vLLM, SGLang and others; the same outputSchema guarantee on a served local model.
A typed prompt language that turns a model's answer into a checked type; another way to write the decision-json adapter.

An open decision control plane: per request picks the model, agent, tool, workflow or human under hard constraints (privacy, region, budget, latency) and explains the choice. Pure Python, no runtime dependencies.
candidates.note: PyPI version 1.10.0 on the day it was read. A router, not a decision model: it compares with decidecall's chain itself, not with one tier.

candidates.what: A local-first, zero-dependency Python model router for agents: utility routing over quality, cost, latency, failure risk, quota and deadline pressure.
candidates.note: 2 stars on the day it was read; small and young. A namesake under MIT for OpenRouter exists at github.com/up2itnow0822/agent-model-router.

candidates.what: JevBench, a public benchmark for Jev-class typed decision models; the yardstick strands-decider and JevK5 report against.
candidates.note: Scores move between versions: every JevBench figure here names its version (v1 for strands-decider's README; v1.4.2.2 for the October 2026 table, where three open 4B models score above Jev).

candidates.what: Claude Haiku through the Claude Code already signed in: `claude -p --model haiku --output-format json --json-schema <schema>` returns `structured_output` that matches the schema.
candidates.note: Flag --json-schema and the field structured_output checked on Claude Code 2.1.288 on 2026-10-02. With --tools "" --strict-mcp-config and a one-line --system-prompt one call reported $0.0037 at list price instead of $0.049 with the default Claude Code system prompt. On a subscription the call uses the plan's limits; the list price is what the same call costs over the API.

candidates.what: Runs an open model on this computer: `ollama run <model> --format json` for the decision-json adapter; POST /api/generate with the output schema as `format` for the strict `ollama` adapter; POST /api/embed (e.g. nomic-embed-text) for the meaning cache.
